look_here_first: Start with an open, wispy annual, heads at several heights, and yellow RAY + DISC florets. For the dangerous Amphiachyris amoena lookalike, inspect SIDE/BACK of phyllaries for possible green nerve borders and especially the tiny DISC-pappus scales. Habit and flower color alone cannot confirm.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Annual, herbaceous single taprooted base; not a woody perennial.
morphology_keys.habit: 10–80(–100) cm, open paniculiform heads at varying heights and wiry photosynthetic branches.
morphology_keys.stems: Green resinous slender glabrous, often angled; lower leaves reduced by flowering.
morphology_keys.leaves: Alternate very narrow, simple, often sessile, resin-gland dotted, reduced distally.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small radiate yellow heads, ray florets around disc florets. FNA species 5–23 rays and 7–48 discs; local variety often about 6–8 rays and 8–13 discs.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: Small overlapping bracts under head; a narrow green nerve border may be visible, but this is VARIABLE and not definitive.
morphology_keys.pappus: Very short scales or effectively absent in local var. texana; Amphiachyris typically has longer conspicuous disc-floret scales. Macro needed.
morphology_keys.fruit: Minute hairy cypsela; retain adult ray-vs-disc assignment before comparing pappus.
best_field_traits: Open, wispy annual rather than woody-based subshrub
Yellow rays and discs; small green resinous branches

comparisons.key_distinctions: A. amoena can also show open arrays. G. texana var. texana has very short/absent disc pappus scales and sometimes a green nerve border on phyllaries; Amphiachyris disc pappus is conspicuous and phyllaries lack the green nerve border. A. dracunculoides is usually more corymbiform. Perennial snakeweed species have woody bases.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Accepted Texas native at Kew; Hays local source. No BONAP/NAPA evidence of 3 project counties fully checked.

taxonomic_scope_note: Kew accepts G. texana and two varieties, var. texana and var. glutinosa; do not assume all species-level observations are variety-confirmed. Do not substitute var. glutinosa Commons photos for local texana variety.
